result.stdout:
Usage: runic-translations import <path> [options]

Import a .resx or i18next catalog into the project's .rmf2 sources.

Reads a .resx file (with its Strings.<locale>.resx satellites) or i18next JSON
(a <lng>.json file, or a directory of <lng>.json or <lng>/<namespace>.json
files) and writes each message into <project>[/<group>]/<locale>.rmf2: keys
become RMF2 names (nested i18next keys become groups), {0}, {name} and {{name}}
become inputs, i18next plural suffixes (_one, _other, ...) become .match on
$count, and .resx comments become descriptions. A message that already exists
keeps its text and translations and is reported as kept; --overwrite replaces
its text with the source's (it keeps its place and comments). Run --dry-run
first. What cannot be mapped is reported per message and the rest is imported.
PO files are not supported: convert them to XLIFF and use xliff import.

Exit codes: 0 success, also when single messages were skipped or refused; 1
command failure, such as an inaccessible file; 2 invalid invocation, a source
that cannot be read, or imported messages that do not compile; 3 internal
failure; 130 cancelled.

Arguments:
  path  The .resx file, or the i18next JSON file or locales directory.
        [required]

Options:
  --from <format>        The source format: resx or i18next. [required]
                         [choices: resx, i18next]
  --project <directory>  Translations directory or its runic.json. Defaults to
                         ./runic.json, then ./translations/runic.json.
  --locale <locale...>   Import only this declared locale; repeatable. Names the
                         locale of a file whose name does not.
  --group <name>         RMF2 group for new messages, written to <group>/.
  --overwrite            Replace the text of messages that already exist;
                         without it they are kept.
  --dry-run              Report the outcome without writing files.
  -h, --help             Show help
  --version              Show version
  --format <human|json>  Select output
[truncated]

result.stdout:
Usage: runic-translations import-text [options]

Import a text-keyed catalog into an RMF2 group.

Generates stable keys from the base texts, writes
<project>/<group>/<locale>.rmf2 and <project>/<group>/base-text.json, then
validates the project. A re-import keeps the key of every base text that is
still present.

Exit codes: 0 success; 1 command failure, such as a verify difference or an
inaccessible file; 2 invalid invocation or translation diagnostics; 3 internal
failure; 130 cancelled.

Options:
  --project <directory>     Translations directory or its runic.json. Defaults
                            to ./runic.json, then ./translations/runic.json.
  --group <name>            RMF2 group, written to <group>/. [required]
  --table <locale=path...>  JSON object mapping base text to translated text for
                            a declared locale; repeatable.
  --base <path>             JSON array of base texts that have no translation
                            yet.
  --dry-run                 Report the files without writing them.
  -h, --help                Show help
  --version                 Show version
  --format <human|json>     Select output format
  @<file>                   Read more arguments from a file

Examples:
  runic-translations import-text --group stored --table de=locales/de.json
  runic-translations import-text --project translations --group stored --base locales/untranslated.json --table de=locales/de.json --dry-run

result.stdout:
Usage: runic-translations status [options]

Report translation coverage per locale.

For every locale: messages translated in the locale, served by a fallback locale
other than the base locale, missing (shown in the base locale), and stale
(translations whose source changed since they were recorded in
<catalog>.review.json, when that file exists). Coverage is translated plus
fallback, as a percentage of the base locale's messages. --min-coverage
<locale>=<percent> (repeatable or comma-separated; * for every translated
locale) fails the command with exit 1 when a locale is below its threshold.

Exit codes: 0 success; 1 a locale is below its --min-coverage, or a file is
inaccessible; 2 invalid invocation, or a catalog whose runic.json, base locale
or translation syntax has errors (run validate); missing translations and the
other validation policies do not stop the report; 3 internal failure; 130
cancelled.

Options:
  --project <directory...>  Translations directory or its runic.json;
                            repeatable. Defaults to ./runic.json, then
                            ./translations/runic.json.
  --min-coverage <locale=percent...>
                            Minimum coverage of a locale, such as de=100,fr=80
                            or *=90; repeatable.
  -h, --help                Show help
  --version                 Show version
  --format <human|json>     Select output format
  @<file>                   Read more arguments from a file

Examples:
  runic-translations status
  runic-translations status --min-coverage de=100,fr=80
  runic-translations status --project src/App/translations --project src/Lib/translations --format json

Usage: runic-translations locale add <tag> [options]

Declare a locale in runic.json and create its empty source files.

Adds the locale to runic.json's locales (as "tag", or { "tag", "fallback" } with
--fallback or when the other entries are objects) and creates an empty
<tag>.rmf2 beside every base-locale .rmf2 file. runic.json keeps its formatting.
The locale starts untranslated: validate reports RTR0010 for each message until
it is translated, or set the locale entry's validation.translationCompleteness
to warning. Nothing is written when the result would not compile.

Exit codes: 0 success; 1 command failure, such as an inaccessible file; 2
invalid invocation, an invalid or declared tag, or translation diagnostics; 3
internal failure; 130 cancelled.

Arguments:
  tag  The BCP 47 locale tag to add, such as fr or de-CH. [required]

Options:
  --fallback <locale>    The declared locale it falls back to; defaults to the
                         base locale.
  --project <directory>  Translations directory or its runic.json. Defaults to
                         ./runic.json, then ./translations/runic.json.
  --dry-run              Report the changes without writing them.
  -h, --help             Show help
  --version              Show version
  --format <human|json>  Select output format
  @<file>                Read more arguments from a file

Examples:
  runic-translations locale add fr
  runic-translations locale add de-CH --fallback de
  runic-translations locale add pt-BR --project src/App/translations --dry-run

Usage: runic-translations locale remove <tag> [options]

Remove a locale from runic.json, delete its source files and its review entries.

Removes the locale's entry from runic.json (keeping its formatting), deletes its
<tag>.rmf2 files or <tag>/ .mf2 files and its entries in <catalog>.review.json.
The base locale and a locale that another locale falls back to cannot be
removed. The files are deleted first, then runic.json is updated; if a file
cannot be deleted, the locale stays declared and the command can be run again.
Use --dry-run to list the files and directories first; files outside the
runic.json directory (from sourceRoots) are marked.

Exit codes: 0 success; 1 command failure, such as an inaccessible file; 2
invalid invocation or a locale that cannot be removed; 3 internal failure; 130
cancelled.

Arguments:
  tag  The declared locale to remove. [required]

Options:
  --project <directory>  Translations directory or its runic.json. Defaults to
                         ./runic.json, then ./translations/runic.json.
  --dry-run              Report the changes without writing or deleting
                         anything.
  -h, --help             Show help
  --version              Show version
  --format <human|json>  Select output format
  @<file>                Read more arguments from a file

Examples:
  runic-translations locale remove fr --dry-run
  runic-translations locale remove fr

result.stdout:
Usage: runic-translations overrides add <catalog> [options]

Scaffold overrides of a library catalog in
translations/overrides/<catalog>/<locale>.rmf2.

Reads the library catalog from the installed package (the restore output's NuGet
package folder, or node_modules), as the build and the Vite plugin find it;
restore first. With --key, adds each message to <locale>.rmf2 seeded with the
library's text in that locale (for a locale the library lacks, the text of the
locale it falls back to), with the library's base text as comments above it, and
records the library text it was written for (the base text and the text that
locale shows) in overrides/<catalog>/<catalog>.review.json, so validate, status,
the Translations Editor and the language server report the override (RTR0090)
when a library update changes either. Without --key, creates <locale>.rmf2 with
every library message as a commented-out template. A locale the library lacks is
added with its first message and falls back to its nearest CLDR parent among the
library's and the added locales, else to the library locale CLDR likely subtags
match, else to the library's base locale. A catalog runic.json does not list in
"overrides" yet is added there, from the package that ships it. The request is
checked first; runic.json, the override source and the review file are then
written together, each only if it did not change meanwhile, or nothing is
written.

Exit codes: 0 success; 1 command failure, such as an inaccessible file; 2
invalid invocation, an unknown catalog, key or locale, or a key that is already
overridden; 3 internal failure; 130 cancelled.

Arguments:
  catalog  The library catalog ID, as runic.json "overrides" lists it, such as
           acme.grid. [required]

Options:
  --locale <tag>         The locale to override, a library locale or one the
                         application adds. [required]
  --key <key...>         A library message to override, as its logical key
                         (grid.title) or canonical key (grid_title); repeatable.
 
[truncated]

Usage: runic-translations review mark [options]

Set the review state of translations against the current source.

Writes <catalog>.review.json beside runic.json (created when missing). Each
entry records the per-unit fingerprint of the current source, so validate warns
(RTR0090) when the source changes later.

Exit codes: 0 success; 1 command failure, such as an inaccessible file; 2
invalid invocation or translation diagnostics; 3 internal failure; 130
cancelled.

Options:
  --project <directory>  Translations directory or its runic.json. Defaults to
                         ./runic.json, then ./translations/runic.json.
  --key <key...>         Message key; repeatable. [required]
  --locale <locale>      A translated locale of the catalog. [required]
  --state <state>        draft, translated, needs-review or approved. [required]
  --note <text>          A review note to store with the entries.
  -h, --help             Show help
  --version              Show version
  --format <human|json>  Select output format
  @<file>                Read more arguments from a file

Examples:
  runic-translations review mark --key greeting --locale de --state approved
  runic-translations review mark --key title --key subtitle --locale fr --state needs-review --note "Check the length."

result.stdout:
Usage: runic-translations xliff export [options]

Write one XLIFF 2.1 document per translated locale.

Writes <catalog>.<locale>.xliff for every locale except the base locale, or only
the --locale ones. Placeholders are <ph> elements with their MF2 expression.
Selector messages (.match, declarations) are one unit: a protected <ph> holds
the declarations and .match, and each variant is a <pc> whose text the
translator edits; a translated locale with other plural categories gets its
variants prefilled in state initial. Messages with markup are exported as
translate="no". Review state comes from <catalog>.review.json beside runic.json,
or --review; a stale approval is exported as needs-review and reported.

Exit codes: 0 success, also when single units were skipped or refused (unless
--fail-on refused); 1 command failure, such as an inaccessible file; 2 invalid
invocation, translation diagnostics, a document that cannot be imported, or a
refused unit with --fail-on refused; 3 internal failure; 130 cancelled.

Options:
  --project <directory>  Translations directory or its runic.json. Defaults to
                         ./runic.json, then ./translations/runic.json.
  --output <directory>   Directory to write the XLIFF documents to. [required]
  --locale <locale...>   Export only this locale; repeatable.
  --review <path>        Review file to read instead of <catalog>.review.json
                         beside runic.json.
  -h, --help             Show help
  --version              Show version
  --format <human|json>  Select output format
  @<file>                Read more arguments from a file

Examples:
  runic-translations xliff export --output xliff
  runic-translations xliff export --project src/App/translations --output xliff --locale de

result.stdout:
Usage: runic-translations xliff import [options]

Import a translated XLIFF document into the .rmf2 or .mf2 sources.

Applies each translated unit to the target locale's sources; untranslated, empty
and markup units are skipped and invalid units refused (a selector unit that
changes its declarations or .match, leaves a variant empty or, under an error
pluralCategories policy, misses the locale's plural categories), each with a
reason, and the rest is applied. A unit whose source changed since export is
applied as needs-review, or refused with --source-changed refuse. Updates
<catalog>.review.json when it exists or --review is given. In CI, --fail-on
refused makes any refused unit fail the command, and then nothing is written.

Exit codes: 0 success, also when single units were skipped or refused (unless
--fail-on refused); 1 command failure, such as an inaccessible file; 2 invalid
invocation, translation diagnostics, a document that cannot be imported, or a
refused unit with --fail-on refused; 3 internal failure; 130 cancelled.

Options:
  --project <directory>      Translations directory or its runic.json. Defaults
                             to ./runic.json, then ./translations/runic.json.
  --source <path>            The XLIFF document to import. [required]
  --source-changed <policy>  needs-review (default) applies a unit whose source
                             changed since export as needs-review; refuse
                             refuses it.
  --review                   Write review state to <catalog>.review.json even
                             when it does not exist yet.
  --fail-on <condition>      refused: fail (exit 2) and write nothing when any
                             unit is refused. By default refused units are
                             warnings and the rest is applied.
  --dry-run                  Report the outcome without writing files.
  -h, --help                 Show help
  --version                  Show version
  --format <human|json>      Select output format
  @<file>        
[truncated]

Selector messages (.match, declarations) are one unit: a protected <ph> holds
the declarations and .match, and each variant is a <pc> whose text the
translator edits; a translated locale with other plural categories gets its
variants prefilled in state initial. Messages with markup are exported as
translate="no". Review state comes from <catalog>.review.json beside runic.json,
or --review; a stale approval is exported as needs-review and reported.

Exit codes: 0 success, also when single units were skipped or refused (unless
--fail-on refused); 1 command failure, such as an inaccessible file; 2 invalid
invocation, translation diagnostics, a document that cannot be imported, or a
refused unit with --fail-on refused; 3 internal failure; 130 cancelled.

Options:
  --project <directory>  Translations directory or its runic.json. Defaults to
                         ./runic.json, then ./translations/runic.json.
  --output <directory>   Directory to write the XLIFF documents to. [required]
  --locale <locale...>   Export only this locale; repeatable.
  --review <path>        Review file to read instead of <catalog>.review.json
                         beside runic.json.
  -h, --help             Show help
  --version              Show version
  --format <human|json>  Select output format
  @<file>                Read more arguments from a file

Examples:
  runic-translations xliff export --output xliff
  runic-translations xliff export --project src/App/translations --output xliff --locale de
